title: A 3D Cell Culture Model Identifies Wnt/β‐Catenin Mediated Inhibition of p53 as a Critical Step during Human Hepatocyte Regeneration

evidence_spans.quote: Here, a 3D spheroid model of PHH is established to study hepatocyte regeneration
experimental methods to expand primary human hepatocytes (PHH)
its proliferative senescence-inducing target PAI1 (SERPINE1)
integrative time-lapse multi-omics analyses

scope_reviewer.uncertainty_reason: The abstract calls PAI1 a senescence-inducing target but does not state that a senescent state or another aging construct was measured, induced, reversed, or compared; it also uses only a generic multi-omics label without naming currently used molecular layers.
scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This is a primary analysis of human hepatocyte regeneration. Cellular senescence is mentioned only as a modifier of a perturbed target while the reported outcomes are regeneration and proliferation, so aging relevance and role are unclear. The generic multi-omics label does not establish two distinct omics layers.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: Activation of Wnt signaling through external cues
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: p53 and PAI1 (SERPINE1) inhibition; primary human hepatocyte proliferation
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Effect of Wnt-signaling activation on p53/PAI1 inhibition and hepatocyte proliferation

adjudication.uncertainty_reason: The abstract does not state that cellular senescence or another aging construct was measured, induced, reversed, or compared; it also does not name two molecular layers despite calling the analysis multi-omics.
adjudication.concise_rationale: This is an empirical biological study of hepatocyte regeneration. PAI1 is described as senescence-inducing, but the analyzed outcomes are p53 inhibition and proliferation rather than a senescent state or other aging construct. Thus the Wnt manipulation cannot serve as a review-specific causal design for aging at title/abstract stage.
